_meta.description:
Deal-scoped activity (ADR-037 fragment). Adds the three relations the LeadDetail tab strip needs and nothing else: task.lead, ticket.lead and contact.leads. Purely additive — no property changes type, none becomes required, and no existing value moves, so the register import needs no breaking-change acknowledgement.

WHY THE CONTACT RELATION SITS ON THE CONTACT. A deal has several stakeholders, so the relation has to be plural. It is modelled as `contact.leads` rather than `lead.contacts` because the object-list widget filters the CHILD schema: `contact?leads=<leadId>` is a query OpenRegister answers with array containment (verified against a live instance — a single-value filter on an array property emits JSON_CONTAINS / jsonb @>), whereas an array held on the lead could only be resolved by filtering `contact` on `id`, and `id` is NOT a filterable field — that request returns EVERY contact and looks like it worked. Carrying it here also answers the question from the other side, which the ContactDetail page asks: which deals is this person on.

`lead.contact` is untouched. It stays the deal's PRIMARY contact, it is what `x-relation-filter` scopes on the lead form, and existing data keeps its meaning.

lead.title: Lead
lead.description: UUID reference to the deal this task belongs to. Set automatically when the task is created from the Tasks tab on a lead — the object-list widget merges its resolved filter into the create payload, so the deal is pre-linked without the user picking it. A task may hang off a client, a request or a deal; the three are independent.

lead.title: Lead
lead.description: UUID reference to the deal this ticket belongs to. Carries a contactmoment (ticketType `interaction`) logged while working a deal, so the conversation history sits with the deal rather than only with the account. Scoped to the deal's own client on the form, because a contact moment about one client's deal never belongs to another client.

leads.title: Leads
leads.description: The deals this person is a stakeholder on. Many-to-many: a deal is worked across several people at an account, and a person carries over from one deal to the next. The lead's own `contact` field names the PRIMARY contact and is a different question — this list is everyone involved.
